oracle_accounting.conceptual_invariant: Caching may reduce evaluator work, but it cannot erase wasteful algorithmic requests. That is why a cache hit still increments oracle_requests.

projected_smoke_cpu_core_hours.GraphGA: PROJECTION, NOT MEASURED. About 820 oracle calls per source, 4100 total. The frozen DRD2 oracle is a numpy RBF-SVM over folded count fingerprints, order milliseconds per molecule; RDKit crossover and mutation dominate at order 10 ms per child. Expect a few minutes wall on one core. Budget 0.1 CPU-core-hours.
projected_smoke_cpu_core_hours.GraphXForm: PROJECTION, NOT MEASURED. 347 MB checkpoint download once. The unit cost is a d=512, 10-block transformer forward for beam 32 on ~25-atom graphs; at roughly 1000 forwards plus 1280 training samples per epoch, expect order 5-10 minutes per epoch per source on a few CPU cores. Budget 2-4 CPU-core-hours for the whole 5-source, 3-epoch smoke, and treat anything beyond 6 as the signal to stop and request GPU authorisation.
projected_smoke_cpu_core_hours.HN_GFN: N/A on CPU. On one V100 the published full loop is 10-13 h; a reduced smoke would be a small fraction of that but is not costable without a run.
projected_smoke_cpu_core_hours.MARS: PROJECTION, NOT MEASURED. Sampler ~0.2 CPU-core-hours. Dominant cost is the one-time vocabulary build over 1,488,640 ChEMBL SMILES with RDKit bond-breaking enumeration, ~0.5-1.0 CPU-core-hours, cacheable to the artifact volume and paid once. Budget 1.5 CPU-core-hours for the first smoke, 0.2 thereafter.
projected_smoke_cpu_core_hours.REINVENT: PROJECTION, NOT MEASURED. Adapter A: an Olivecrona-style RNN sampling 64 SMILES of ~60 tokens per step on CPU, order seconds per step; ~20 steps per source gives a few minutes each, so budget 0.3 CPU-core-hours for 5 sources plus a small prior download. Adapter B: transformer priors are larger; budget 0.5-1.0 CPU-core-hours plus the Zenodo prior downloads. Total 1.0-1.5 CPU-core-hours.
